title: Paper sprint scrapbook — inference ideas & experiments
content:
Goal: keep a compact, messy log of papers, quick takeaways, and small experiment ideas that could map back to runtime improvements or Eval probes. Not a polished literature review — more of a 2–4 hour sprint capture for followups.

Quick index (things to skim later):
- kernel selection & late binding ideas (paper: kernel-match-rl-ish)
- asymmetric KV compression + cheap probes for degradation
- low-bit fold-in strategies for attention + perf tradeoffs
- microbenchmarks to reproduce: tiled attention vs fused kernels on A100/RTX; short-context heavy tail throughput

Notes to self: what matters for Redwood product teams:
- measurable SLO impact: latency p50/p99 change, cost per token variance; make any idea map to these metrics first.
- fallback story: any perf improv that occasionally degrades quality must include a cheap detection/eval hook.
- integration surface: is this a serving-runtime change, or precompile/optimizer thing? that decides review path.

Papers skimmed (very rough)
1) "Adaptive Kernel Routing for Transformer Inference" (arXiv:xxxx.xxxx) -- idea: at runtime choose kernel variant per-layer or per-seq-length using a tiny policy network.
   - takeaways: single-model can route to either low-memory fused path or high-throughput tiled path; decision cost must be amortized.
   - experiment: add a micro policy that routes by current token count mod batch size and compare latency/cost on 4 workload distributions (short, medium, long, mixed).
   - redwood mapping: useful for Dedicated autoscaler to squeeze more throughput when tail latency headroom exists.

2) "Quantized KV-store with Asymmetric Compression" (conference slides)
   - idea: compress KV cache with different quant/preshift per head; store compact indices. Improves memory bound cases.
   - unresolved: how does lossy kv compression affect coherence for long contexts? Need an eval harness with grounding prompts.
   - experiment: simulate 8-bit vs 4-bit asymmetric compression on GPT-style kv for 32k context. Measure next-token cross-entropy drift and downstream QA accuracy on long-context tasks.

3) "Late-binding kernel compilation for dynamic shapes"
   - takeaway: JIT-compile several kernel variants and pick at runtime based on batch shape distro. Compilation overhead dominated first-run; cache warmed by model spin-ups.
   - practical note: precompile warm pool during model load for Dedicated instances to avoid first-request hiccups.

4) "Tiny inference policies: bandit-based batching"
   - summary: use lightweight bandit to pick batch sizes per route to stay below latency SLO while maximizing throughput.
   - experiment: implement epsilon-greedy batch-size selector in bench harness, feed synthetic workloads (bursty, steady, poisson). Compare cost per effective token and p99 latency.

Short-form experiments I want to run (cheap):
- micro-bench: fused vs tiled attention on 1/2/4 GPUs for seq lens 64/512/4096, measure tokens/sec and p99. Shell script + torchscript. Ticket: JIRA-RI-1938 (create perf harness)
- kv-compression sim: wrapper around cached KV arrays, quantize with different schemes, replay recorded request traces from prod anonymized bucket. Metrics: CE drift, QA F1 on long-doc retrievals.
- cheap-detector: build a delta-entropy heuristic that flags when quantized-kv likely to drift; test on synthetic hallucination cases.

Ideas & one-liners to bring to sync with Priya:
- "lazy precompile" during model upload: kick off precompilation on Dedicated to reduce warm-start latency. Rollout: default off, opt-in via model tag.
- "adaptive-batching-as-a-service" policy in the control plane that can be tuned per-customer by traffic shape.
- small eval suite: 100 prompt templates sensitive to kv degradation (dialog with entity tracking + document patching).

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How much of kernel switching is limited by PCIe/PCIe contends vs compute? Need system-level profiling.
- Cache formats: is the architecture-level alignment going to wreck asymmetric compression gains on certain GPUs/DPUs?
- Can we roll our own cheap policy without central control-plane churn? (edge-case customers on Private need low-change footprint)

Link stash (to revisit):
- arXiv placeholders I kept during sprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxx, https://arxiv.org/abs/yyyy.yyyy
- internal slack thread: https://redwoodworkspace.slack.com/archives/C12345/p1640000000000
- draft confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/adaptive-kernel-routing-notes

Todo (next 2 weeks):
- (High) wire up micro-bench script and run on dedicated dev rig. Attach results to JIRA-RI-1938.
- (Med) design 50-template eval for kv-degradation and get Priya to sanity-check templates.
- (Low) sketch a short internal slide: 4 slides (motivation, ideas, experiments, ask). Bring to eng sync.

Random scribbles:
- could we piggyback some of the detection on token-level entropies we already capture in Console? If so, cheaper rollout.
- consider using per-route short-term learning (bandit) but need guardrails to avoid oscillations.

End of sprint dump. Keep messy — will prune after experiments.
